chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Adam ibn Ishaq, from a man, from Isa ibn A'yan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who gave a gift to another man while hoping for its reward (in return or as charity), but the recipient did not compensate him or return it until he died, and the man obtained his gift in kind. Is it permissible for him to take it back if he is able to do so? He (AS) said, 'There is no harm in him taking it.'
ai.seo_question: Can a giver reclaim a gift if the recipient dies without fulfilling the expected reciprocity?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a gift given with the hope of reciprocity (*thawab*) remains revocable if the recipient dies without fulfilling that expectation, allowing the giver to reclaim the specific item. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between a pure charitable gift (*hibah*) and one given with an implicit condition of return, emphasizing that the failure of the expected return preserves the giver's right to restitution. It underscores the practical application of fairness in social transactions, ensuring that the giver is not left with a loss when the intended spiritual or social benefit is not realized.
